DRAFTING AND PATTERN MAKING
5.1
INTRODUCTION
Drafting
and making
a paper pattern for a garment
is an art. There are various stages in
garment making such as taking measurements,
observing the body for special adjustment
needs, drafting the garment, cutting a paper pattern, etc. The major work is translating the
drafting into a garment. It is important
to draft the garment properly in order to get a well
fitting garment.
Let us now see what is meant by drafting,
why it needs to be done and
how it can be done.
5.2
Objective
After reading this lesson, you will be able to dothe
following:
•
make a drafting
and paper pattern correctly;
•
explain the need and advantages
of drafting
and making
a paper pattern;
•
cut the pattern properly.
5.3
MEANING
AND NEED
Meaning of drafting
The basic draft of the garment, which is made on cloth or paper according to body
measurements
taken, is known as 'drafting'.

50 :: Home Science
A)
Need for drafting
1.
For a good fit
In order to get a good fit in the final garment, it is necessary to make a drafting.
The drafting is made according to the body measurements
and this to a large
extent, determines the fitting ofthe garment.
2.
To save time
Drafting saves time because any defects can be corrected at this stage itself and .
one does not waste time in ripping out and stitching the garment again to correct
defects.
3.
Prevents
alteration
Since the drafting is made very carefully,there are less chances ofthe final garment
needing any alteration.
b)
Types of drafting
Drafting can be done in two ways.
1.
Scale drawing
The drafting which is made on a reduced scale, in a note book, is called a scale
drawing (drafting).
2.
Drafting
The drafting of the garment is made on cloth, paper or milton cloth according to
measurement taken. A good drafting ensures a well fitting garment and hence is
very important.
Meaning
of paper pattern
A paper pattern is made after the drafting. When the drafting made on brown
paper or newspaper is cut along the lines ofthe drafting, it is called a paper pattern.
c)
Need for paper pattern
Making a paper pattern before cutting the cloth has the following advantages:-
1.
Saves time
Ifwe have to make more than one garment of the same size, the same paper
p~ttem can be used which saves time.

Drafting
and Pattern Making

2.
Fault removal
Any defect which may occur can be corrected at the time of making the paper
pattern.
3.
Designing
Variousdesigns can be tried out on the pattern itself to find out which is the suitable
one. This makes designing on the fabric easier.
4.
Layout
It becomes easy to layout the pattern on the cloth. In this way, we can easily
estimate the amount of cloth needed and optimise the utilisation ofthe cloth by
laying out all the pieces of the pattern correctly. Any wastage of cloth and errors
while cutting is thus minimised.
5.
Maintain records
The paper pattern developed for any particular person can be kept and the same
could be used for stitching other garments for that person without having to take
fresh measurements.
5.4
DRAFTING AND PAPER PATTERN MAKING
a)
Drafting
The following points should be kept in mind while drafting:
1.
Have all the tools needed ready before starting.
2.
Ensure you have the correct measurements.
3.
Use a large table or a board for drafting.
4.
While drafting on a paper use the paper in the vertical direction.
5.
Pin the paper on the drafting board using drafting pins.
6.
Leave a margin of 1" on all sides while drafting on a paper.
7.
First of all, draw the 'base line' along the longer side of the paper.
8.
Draw the other base lines perpendicular to the base line. These lines are the 'top
line' and the 'bottom line'. The bottom line is always to the left and the top line
should always be to the right.

(b)
Making a paper pattern
When the drafting is cut carefully alongthe outer lines, it is known as 'patterri'.The pattern
is placed on the cloth before cutting. It is important to keep the following points in mind.
Keep the note book with measurements nearby for ready reference.
The pattern should be of the actual size ofthe garment to be made.
The drafting should be made on the rough side ofthe paper.
The extra or useless lines on the drafting should be cancelled out with the help of
chalk.
Always use a full-scale to make the drafting on paper.
While making a pattern keep allowances for seams, turning, in-lays, etc.
Set the design to be made on the pattern itself.

(c)
Cutting the pattern
1.
Check the entire pattern carefully before cutting.
2.
Cut the pattern carefully along the lines.
3.
Make use of 'balances' and 'notches' on the pattern. This will facilitate the transfer
of marks for pockets, darts, etc. on to the cloth.
4.
Make equal notches.
5.
Cut all the parts of the pattern very carefully.
6.
Keep all the parts of the pattern in a brown paper envelop and note down the
description and other information on top ofthe envelop.

5.5
TYPES OF PAPER PATTERN
I
There can be various types of paper patterns as exp lained below:
Wi.
IH.
1.
Ordinary Pattern
The pattern which is first cut is known as the ordinary pattern. This pattern can
be cut according to standard measuremdents
or according to specific given
measurements.
2.
Individual Pattern
The pattern cut according to the measurements of an individual is known as an
individual pattern. This type of pattern can not be used for any other individual.

· Drafting
and Pattern
Making
:: 55
3.
Readymade or Bought Pattern
These are available only in foreign countries. These are sold in various standard
sizes. Women in foreign countries know how to sew but not how to cut. Therefore,
it becomes convenient to buy the pattern ofthe correct size and use it at home.
4.
Final Pattern
The pattern which is perfect in all respects and free from all defects is known as
the final pattern. The final pattern is made after the customer has tried on the
garment and the defects observed are corrected in the pattern.
5.
Block Pattern
The patternmade accordingto givenmeasurements with onlythe standard looseness
is known as the block pattern. This kind of pattern has no other allowances such
as for seams, turning, overlap, etc. Only the darts and the balance mark are put
on the block pattern.
6.
Graded Pattern
The pattern which has different sizes marked on it is known as a graded pattern.
For example, chest sizes of32", 34", 36" maybe marked on one pattern itself.
There is a difference of2" between successive sizes. The pattern can be cut
according to the size required.
7.
Dress Pattern
The pattern made with the design, seam allowance, turning, inlay, overlap, etc.,
is known, as a dress pattern.
